item.title: Measuring What Matters from a Macromarketing Perspective
item.content:encoded:
M. Joseph Sirgy, Virginia Tech

Ben Wooliscroft, Auckland University of Technology

This special issue focuses on developing macromarketing metrics that measure marketing's societal impact across various domains. Similar to how other disciplines employ standardized indicators—such as GDP in economics or life expectancy in healthcare—the call invites scholars to create comprehensive metrics capturing both positive and negative effects of marketing on society. The issue builds on existing academic and public sector measures and seeks to expand the toolkit for evaluating marketing's contribution to social well-being.

Submissions may examine metrics spanning multiple contexts including consumer vulnerability, sustainable practices, quality of life improvements, socio-economic development, and emerging issues like artificial intelligence and climate change. Both empirical and conceptual papers are welcomed, with particular encouragement for conceptual work that could guide future research. The special issue aims to generate metrics useful for both policy regulation and managerial decision-making across industries, sectors, and social groups.

Appel publié par Journal of Macromarketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Marketing systems' efficiency and effectiveness
  • Marketing's role in socio-economic development
  • Empirical distributive justice
  • Marketing of products and services that enhance quality of life
  • Non-WEIRD consumption norms and impacts
  • Non-traditional consumption and quality of life
  • Consumer vulnerability in disadvantaged groups
  • Sustainable consumption
  • Sustainable production and supply practices
  • Marketing contribution to peace and conflict mitigation
  • Symmetry of trade benefits between nations and channels
  • Health promotion contribution to consumer segments
  • Marketing and climate change mitigation
  • Artificial intelligence's impact on marketing and well-being

Timeline

  • July 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Is Progress Possible Without People? Navigating Quality of Life Between Homo Sapiens and Homo Digitalis
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the tension between human wellbeing and technological advancement in contemporary society. It investigates how progress can be defined and achieved when considering the interplay between traditional human values and the emerging digital dimension of human existence, asking whether societal advancement necessarily requires prioritizing technological development over human quality of life.

The issue invites contributions that explore socio-economic dimensions of human-digital coexistence, considering how societies can navigate the balance between innovation and maintaining or enhancing quality of life for human populations.

Appel publié par Socio-Economic Planning Sciences. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Quality of life

item.title: Enhancing Population Health Assessment: Key Papers from the EQ-DAPHNIE Project
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Lapin, Cleveland Clinic

Jessica Roydhouse, Menzies Institute for Medical Research

The EQ-DAPHNIE project, funded by the EuroQol Research Foundation, conducted a comprehensive population health assessment across 15 countries, collecting demographic data, social determinants of health, and diverse patient-reported outcome measures. This special collection brings together research examining the findings from this initiative.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Establishment of population norms for patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs)
  • Cross-country comparisons of health measures
  • Examination of health inequalities across populations
  • Assessment of instrument performance within and across countries
  • Self-reported health measures and analysis
  • Efficacy of different measures in elderly populations
  • Evaluation of generic and symptom-specific PROMs

item.title: Patient experience data in regulatory and health technology assessment
item.content:encoded:
Wen-Hung Chen, AstraZeneca

Lori D. McLeod, RTI Health Solutions

Regulatory and health technology assessment bodies increasingly recognize the value of incorporating patient perspectives during product development and evaluation. Patient experience data encompasses patient-reported outcomes, clinical assessments, and preference information, yet their integration into decision-making remains inconsistent. This collection seeks to advance understanding of how different stakeholders approach patient experience data to ensure patient voices meaningfully influence healthcare decisions.

The collection invites original research, reviews, and discussion papers examining how patient experience data—including preferences, symptoms, and quality of life measures—can inform regulatory and HTA submissions and decisions. Contributions addressing recent developments in the field and exploring emerging applications such as artificial intelligence and digital health technologies in patient experience research are particularly encouraged.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Assessment of patient experience, preferences, symptoms, and health-related quality of life for regulatory and HTA submissions
  • Patient-reported outcomes and clinical outcome assessments in product development and evaluation
  • Patient preference information collection and evaluation
  • Artificial intelligence and digital health technology applications in patient experience data research
  • Regulatory and HTA developments and decision-making processes
  • Integration of patient voices in healthcare decisions to improve patient outcomes

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Submission deadline
